title: The Golden Calf and the Samiri

paragraphs.text: Pharaoh misled his people. Allah saved the Children of Israel from their enemy and sent them manna and quails. He told them to eat the good things and not go beyond limits, or His anger would fall on them. But Allah keeps forgiving whoever repents, believes, does good and stays guided.

Moses hurried ahead of his people to meet Allah, hoping to please Him. Allah told him that his people had been tested, and the Samiri had led them astray. Moses went back angry and sad. He asked if the promise had seemed too long, or if they wanted Allah's anger, since they broke their promise to him. They said they did not break it by choice. They had carried heavy jewelry of the people and threw it into the fire, as the Samiri did.

The Samiri made them a calf statue that made a sound. They claimed it was the deity of Moses too, and that he had forgotten. Could they not see it could not answer them or bring harm or benefit? Aaron had warned them it was a test and told them to follow him. But they said they would keep worshipping it until Moses returned.

Moses asked Aaron why he did not stop them. Aaron said, "O son of my mother, do not hold my beard or my head. I feared you would say I divided the Children of Israel." Then Moses asked the Samiri what he had done.

hardWords.m: rings, chains and other gold things worn for beauty
a shape of a person or animal made of metal or stone
hair on a man's chin and face
